984.text: Populous EncyclopaediaWelcome to the Populous Encyclopaedia.This Encyclopaedia is an extension of the Populous manual. It lists in detail each spell, building and Follower which you have gained while you have been playing the game. Each time you discover a new spell, it will appear in the Encyclopaedia and you will be able to learn how to use it easily and quickly. The same will happen with new buildings and Followers.Click on each heading on the Main Menu to bring up the list of topics in that section. Then, click on each topic to bring up further information. For example, if you want to learn about the Guard Tower building, left-click on the Buildings heading to bring up the Buildings Menu and then left-click on Guard Tower to view all the information about the Guard Tower.

985.text: The WorldManaTrees and WoodWaterReincarnation SiteStone HeadObeliskVault of KnowledgeTotem PoleWildmenBoatsBalloons

986.text: Trees and WoodOn every world you play, you will see trees dotted around the landscape. Trees are very important to you because you need them for every type of construction, from buildings to boats. You can Gather Wood from trees by selecting one or more of your Braves (the only Followers who can construct buildings and vehicles) and Left Clicking on a tree. Each tree contains up to four pieces of wood. The less wood it has, the smaller it is and if you gather all the pieces of wood, it will be uprooted and disappear. Trees do grow back to full health but it does take a while so make sure you don't run out prematurely. If you do, you may have to hunt for more.The wood you gather can be dropped anywhere and your Braves will drop it if they have nothing else to do. Your Braves will gather wood from trees automatically when you command them to construct something, but they will always use any nearby piles of wood before cutting down a tree.

987.text: <t>Water</t><r><r>Water in Populous is fatal and, although your Followers avoid it, they will drown if they fall in.

988.text: Reincarnation SiteThe Reincarnation Site is your source of power on each world. The stones of the site channel all the Mana gathered from your Followers and you can draw on this power to cast powerful and destructive spells.When you begin a world, a Reincarnation Site will be created and your struggle for supremacy will begin. If the Shaman dies and you have lost all your Followers, the Reincarnation Site will be destroyed and the level will be over. If you die and you still have Followers on the world however, the Shaman will be reincarnated in the Stone Circle.You can't cast spells on an Enemy Reincarnation Site and the only way to destroy one is to defeat the entire Enemy tribe. Your Reincarnation Site can be used as the starting point of a settlement.

989.text: Stone HeadStone Heads are mystical statues left on the worlds by The Ancients. If they are worshipped, they will reward you with new skills that you can use to conquer the Enemy. Powers gained from Stone Heads only provide a single use, but more can be accumulated. If the new skill is a spell, you will only be able to cast it once, and if it is a building, you will only be able to construct it once.If you right-click on a Stone Head, it will show you how many of your Followers are needed to worship the stone to begin. When a Stone Head is completely drained, it will sink into the ground.To worship a Stone Head, select some Followers and left-click on the Stone Head. If you right-click on the Stone Head again, you will see a red line next to the number of Followers and this indicates how long it will take. Once it has finished, you will receive the new skill, although your Followers will keep worshipping until you command them to stop.

990.text: <t>The Vault of Knowledge</t><r><r>These ancient Vaults are tall buildings which store the knowledge of an Enemy Shaman. The symbol at the top of the building indicates the type of knowledge contained within the structure. If the Shaman gains entry to a Vault, the Enemy's knowledge will pass to her permanently.<r><r>Select the Shaman and left-click on the vault to begin. Remember that the Vault of Knowledge will often be heavily guarded.

991.text: Totem PoleTotem Poles are magical devices which, when worshipped, trigger a spell. This spell will often grant the player access to previously unreachable parts of the world, or cause massive devastation to the Enemy.If you right-click on the Totem Pole, it will show you how many of your Followers are needed to worship that Totem Pole to begin.To worship a Totem Pole, select some Followers and left-click on the pole. If you right-click on the pole again, you will see a red line next to the number of Followers and this indicates how long it will take.

992.text: WildmenOn every world are native Wildmen who wander the land scavenging for food and water. Although they pose no threat to you, they can be converted to your cause to swell the ranks of your army.To do this, you must cast the Convert spell on them to convert them into Braves. There are only a limited number of Wildmen on each world so you must do your best to convert them before the Enemy does.

993.text: BoatsBoats are constructed in the Boat House by your Braves and are used to navigate the otherwise impassable oceans of the world. To start producing Boats, send some Braves into the Boat House (by selecting them and Left Clicking on the building). The Braves will then gather wood and begin construction. When a Boat is constructed, a Brave will then sail it to the shore next to the Boat House.You can place up to five Followers in each Boat. To put a Follower in a Boat, select the Follower and left-click on the Boat. If you have more than one Boat, you can hold down the Ctrl key and left-click on each Boat in turn to put multiple Followers in them. To move a Boat, select the Boat or a Follower inside and left-click anywhere on the water. If you left-click on dry land, the Boat will beach but your Followers will not disembark. To make your Followers disembark, right-click on the Boat and left-click on the Disembark icon.

994.text: BalloonsBalloons enable you to travel to any location on world with ease. They are constructed in the Balloon Hut by your Braves and can carry up to two Followers. To start producing Balloons, send some Braves into the Balloon Hut (by selecting them and Left Clicking on the building). The Braves will then gather wood and begin construction. When a new Balloon is produced, one Brave will get into the Balloon and fly it outside the building.To put a Follower in a Balloon, select the Follower and left-click on the Balloon. If you have more than one Balloon, you can hold down the Ctrl key and left-click on each Balloon in turn to put multiple Followers in them. To move a Balloon, select the Balloon of a Follower inside and left-click anywhere on the world. To make your Followers disembark, right-click on the Balloon and left-click on the Disembark icon.The additional height of the Balloon over the land gives you an added advantage when casting most spells.

996.text: HutThe Hut is a unique building which you can construct to house your Followers. When your Braves are in their Huts, they are hidden from the Enemy's sight and also generate Mana for you. When an individual Hut has been occupied for a while, your Braves will upgrade it to a Medium Hut which can hold up to four people. Then, when it has been occupied for a while more, it will be upgraded to a Large Hut which can hold up to five Followers. Each stage also increases the amount of Mana produced by the occupants. You need one or more Followers in a Hut for it to create new Braves. The more Followers you have in the Hut, the faster this will be.First Stage:Wood Required to ConstructMax Number of OccupantsAmount of Mana ProducedBirth TimeStrengthSecond Stage:Wood Required to ConstructMax Number of OccupantsAmount of Mana ProducedBirth TimeStrengthThird Stage:Wood Required to ConstructMax Number of OccupantsAmount of Mana ProducedBirth TimeStrength

997.text: Guard TowerThe Guard Tower is a unique building which can be placed anywhere on the landscape to give you an advanced warning of an Enemy attack. Any Follower placed inside the tower will sound a warning bell whenever an Enemy Follower approaches. You can then zoom to the Tower by pressing the Space Bar.Since the Guard Tower does not need to be constructed next to an existing building, it can also be used to begin a new settlement. Because of the height of the tower, any Follower placed inside has improved abilities.Shamans can fire spells further, Braves extend the look-out range, Warriors will call for help to defend the settlement, Firewarriors can fire further, Preachers can preach further and Spies can unmask Enemy Spies. Building the Guard Tower on top of high ground will extend these ranges even further.Wood Required to ConstructMax Number of OccupantsStrength

998.text: Warrior Training HutThe Warrior Training Hut is used to train Braves or other Followers into Warriors, stronger and hardier Followers who enjoy Guarding and Attacking. Once you have constructed the Warrior Training Hut, you can train your Followers by selecting any number of them and Left Clicking on the building.Your Followers will then line up outside and enter one by one to be trained. Training also requires Mana so if your Followers are not entering the building, you may not have enough Mana to train them.Wood Required to ConstructMax Number of OccupantsStrength

999.text: TempleThe Temple is used to train Braves or other Followers into Preachers, Followers who can Preach to the Enemy and convert them to your cause. Once you have constructed the Temple, you can train your Followers by selecting any number of them and Left Clicking on the building. Your Followers will then line up outside and enter one by one to be trained. Training also requires Mana so if your Followers are not entering the building, you may not have enough Mana to train them.Wood Required to ConstructMax Number of OccupantsStrength

1000.text: Spy Training HutThe Spy Training Hut is used to train Braves or other Followers into Spies, subversive Followers who can disguise themselves as the Enemy and sabotage their buildings. Once you have constructed the Spy Training Hut, you can train your Followers by selecting any number of them and Left Clicking on the building. Your Followers will then line up outside and enter one by one to be trained. Training also requires Mana so if your Followers are not entering the building, you may not have enough Mana to train them.Wood Required to ConstructMax Number of OccupantsStrength

1001.text: Firewarrior Training HutThe Firewarrior Training Hut is used to train Braves or other Followers into Firewarriors, Followers with the ability to throw devastating fireballs at the Enemy and their buildings. Once you have constructed the Firewarrior Training Hut, you can train your Followers by selecting any number of them and Left Clicking on the building. They will then line up outside and enter one by one to be trained. Training also requires Mana so if your Followers are not entering the building, you may not have enough Mana to train them.Wood Required to ConstructMax Number of OccupantsStrength

1002.text: Boat HouseThe Boat House allows you to construct Boats capable of holding up to five Followers. Boat Houses have to be positioned carefully because they can only back up onto water and also have to be next to an existing building. When you are placing one down, choose a bit of coastline that is straight and flat. Rotate the Boat House Plan with the Space Bar so that the entrance is facing away from the water. If the Plan is in a valid position (and you have a building nearby, such as a Guard Tower), you can place it down and begin construction. If you do not, you will have to find an alternative site.To start producing Boats, send some Braves into the Boat House (by selecting them and Left Clicking on the building). The Braves will then gather wood and begin construction. When a new Boat is produced, one Brave will then sail it round to the shore next to the Boat House.Wood Required to Construct buildingWood required to Construct BoatMax Number of OccupantsStrength

1003.text: Balloon HutThe Balloon Hut enables you to construct Balloons capable of flying anywhere on the world. Balloon Huts are large and use a lot of wood, so be careful where you build them.To start producing Balloons, send some Braves into the Balloon Hut (by selecting them and Left Clicking on the building). The Braves will gather wood and begin construction. When a new Balloon is produced, one Brave will get into the Balloon and fly it outside the building.Wood Required to Construct buildingWood required to Construct BoatMax Number of OccupantsStrength

1004.text: Guard PostA Guard Post allows you to guard and patrol areas of your settlement and the surrounding area. They do not require wood to build, can be placed anywhere and any Follower can be commanded to use them. To use a Guard Post, first place one down on the landscape and select some of your Followers. Then left-click on the Guard Post and your Followers will run to it and circle it.You can also set down more than one Guard Post and tell your Followers to move between them, thus creating a patrol. Place down two more Guard Posts and select your Followers. Then hold down Ctrl and left-click on each Guard Post in turn, stopping on the last one. Your Followers will now run between all the Guard Posts and return to the first when the last is reached.You can perform even more complex actions using Guard Posts. If you hold down Ctrl and send one or more of your Followers to a Guard Post and then set them some more actions, such as chopping down a tree, they will only go to the Guard Post. When you are ready, you can press the n key, your Followers will stop guarding and perform their next commands; in this case, chopping down a tree. This allows you to synchronise your Followers and perform many tasks at once, all triggered at once by pressing the n key.Your Guard Posts are invisible to the Enemy and the Enemy's are invisible to you.To remove a Guard Post, hold down Shift and right-click on it.

1006.text: BlastThe Blast spell is your simplest offensive weapon. When fired, it creates a ball of flame and a shockwave which hurls any nearby people into the air, including your own Followers. Be careful when using this spell near water.To Use: Left-click to select the Blast Spell from the Spells Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell. Left-click to fire.RangeMana Required

1007.text: ConvertThe Convert spell is a special spell which you can cast around Wildmen to convert them to your cause. When you cast the spell, a ring of light will appear and any chosen Wildmen inside the ring will be converted.To Use: Left-click to select the Convert spell from the Spells Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell. Left-click to fire.RangeMana Required

1008.text: Ghost ArmyThe Ghost Army spell creates ethereal Followers for you to command. Although they have no strength and cannot perform any tasks, such as construction, they appear solid and real to the Enemy. You can command them as you do normal Followers but as soon as they are hurt in any way, they will disappear in a cloud of smoke.If you cast the Ghost Army spell on an empty piece of ground, you will create ghost Braves. If you cast the spell on another Follower, however, you will create a ghost of that Follower (i.e. cast the Ghost Army spell on a Shaman and you create ghost Shamans). This spell is only available during multiplayer games.To Use: Left-click to select the Ghost Army spell from the Spells Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell. Left-click to fire.RangeMana Required

1009.text: SwarmSwarm creates a cloud of stinging insects, which will attack Enemy Followers and buildings. If a swarm attacks an Enemy Follower, he will run away from the cloud of insects. If the swarm attacks a building, any Followers inside will be forced out and away from the settlement. The swarm will also cause some damage to Enemy Followers.To Use: Left-click to select the Swarm spell from the Spells Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell. Left-click to fire.RangeMana Required

1010.text: InvisibilityThe Invisibility spell enables you to turn some of your Followers invisible for a period of time. If you fire it at a point on the ground, any Followers within a short distance will be turned invisible. The Shaman is immune to the spell and cannot use it on herself.To Use: Left-click to select the Invisibility spell from the Spells Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell. Left-click to fire.RangeMana Required

1011.text: Land BridgeThe Land Bridge spell, when cast on the far shore of a stretch of water separating two pieces of land, will join those pieces of land by raising the ocean floor. You can also use the spell to create a ramp up to the top of a cliff by standing at the bottom and casting the spell on the top; or you can join two hills together to make a handy defence platform.To Use: Find two pieces of land separated by a small stretch of water and move your Shaman to the edge of one shore. Left-click to select the Land Bridge spell from the Spells Panel and move the mouse pointer so that it is on the edge of the opposite shore. Left-click to fire.RangeMana Required

1012.text: LightningLightning is a more powerful version of the Blast spell. When cast, a lightning bolt will strike the earth and kill or set fire to anything it touches, including Enemy Followers, trees and buildings.To Use: Left-click to select the Lightning spell from the Spells Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell. Left-click to fire.RangeMana Required

1013.text: HypnotiseHypnotise, when cast on Enemy Followers, converts anyone (except Shamans) to your tribe for a short period of time. Like the Invisibility spell, it only affects those within a short distance of where the spell was fired. The Shaman is immune to the spell.To Use: Left-click to select the Hypnotise spell from the Spells Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell. Left-click to fire.RangeMana Required

1014.text: TornadoThe Tornado spell creates a destructive force of dust and wind which destroys anything in its path. If any Followers are caught in it's path, they will be picked up and flung across the land. If the Tornado hits any buildings, they will be pulled apart and destroyed. Since Tornadoes are a force of nature, you have no control over their path, so bear this in mind when you cast one.To Use: Left-click to select the Tornado spell from the Spells Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell. Left-click to fire.RangeMana Required

1015.text: SwampWhen cast upon a piece of ground, Swamp causes the ground to become a deep bog capable of swallowing up anything which runs into it, including your own Followers.To Use: Left-click to select the Swamp spell from the Spells Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell. Left-click to fire. Right-click on any of your Swamps to find out how many more people that Swamp can swallow. Hold down Shift and Right-click on any of your Swamps to remove them.RangeMana Required

1016.text: FlattenFlatten is a powerful land-altering spell which, when cast on a piece of land, will spread out and level the land around to the same height as the point it was cast on.To Use: Left-click to select the Flatten spell from the Spells Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell. Left-click to fire.RangeMana Required

1017.text: EarthquakeThe Earthquake spell tears the land apart and can be a very devastating spell when used against the Enemy on high ground.To Use: Left-click to select the Earthquake spell from the Spells Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell. Left-click to fire.RangeMana Required

1018.text: ErodeErode allows you to accelerate time and weather an area of land as if water were shaping and eroding the rock. This can cause the Enemy's buildings to sink into the water, or make ravines smooth and navigable.To Use: Left-click to select the Erode spell from the Spells Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell. Left-click to fire.RangeMana Required

1019.text: FirestormThe Firestorm spell turns rain into fire and balls of flame fall to earth. This is a powerful spell, devastating against buildings and people.To Use: Left-click to select the Firestorm spell from the Spells Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell. Left-click to fire.RangeMana Required

1020.text: Angel Of DeathThe Angel Of Death is a demonic serpent who will hunt out Enemy Followers and destroy them.To Use: Left-click to select the Angel Of Death spell from the Spells Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell. Left-click to fire.RangeMana Required

1021.text: VolcanoThe Volcano spell is the most powerful spell in your arsenal and can lay waste to huge tracts of the landscape. It uses a large amount of Mana, but once cast will prove your domination over the Enemy.To Use: Left-click to select the Volcano spell from the Spells Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell. Left-click to fire.RangeMana Required

1023.text: ShamanIn Populous: The Beginning you play the Shaman, guiding her to the ultimate goal of becoming a deity and gaining god-like omnipotence. If you are killed you will reincarnate at the Reincarnation Site, but only if you have other Followers converted to your faith. If you do not have any Followers on the world, you will die and lose the game.The Shaman will not perform menial tasks. Instead, she is skilled in magic allowing her to cast the spells available on the Spells Panel. To cast one of these spells, you have to walk to within range of the target. Each spell has a different range. When you select a spell from the Spells Panel, a mystical force will surround the Shaman indicating the boundaries of the spell's range. You can then left-click within the range to cast the spell.You can also command your Followers to guard the Shaman. Select some of your Followers and press g. Those Followers will then run to the Shaman and surround her, attacking any Enemy who tries to reach her. To stop them guarding, deselect any followers and press g again.When a Shaman dies, a quarter of her Mana will be taken from her and given to the tribe who killed her.LifeStrengthAbilitiesThe Shaman is the conduit for your destructive spells and powers. Available spells are: Blast, Convert, Magical Shield, Ghost Army, Swarm, Invisibility, Land Bridge, Lightning, Hypnotise, Bloodlust, Teleport, Tornado, Swamp, Flatten, Earthquake, Erode, Firestorm, Angel of Death, Volcano, ArmageddonList of possible commandsWalk to point, Attack Enemy, Attack Enemy building, Enter Hut, Guard, Enter boat, Enter balloon, Worship Object

1024.text: BraveThe Brave is your basic Follower and the workhorse of your settlements. They construct your buildings and can be trained to become more powerful with new abilities. Braves prefer to build and live in houses where they can breed more Braves. You must have a sufficient number of Huts for your Followers and they will stop breeding if you do not. Since Braves are the only Follower who can construct and gather wood, it is always a good idea to keep a few around just in case you need them.LifeStrengthAbilitiesCollect wood for construction, construct buildingsList of possible commandsWalk to point, Attack Enemy, Attack Enemy building, Construct Building, Enter Hut, Gather wood, Pick up wood, Guard, Enter boat, Enter balloon, Worship Object

1025.text: WarriorWarriors are created by training Braves or any other Follower in the Warrior Training Hut. These improved fighters are much stronger in battle than the Brave. They do not perform menial tasks, such as construction, and are best suited to Guarding or Fighting.LifeStrengthAbilitiesGuarding, fightingList of possible commandsWalk to point, Attack Enemy, Attack Enemy building, Enter Hut, Guard, Enter boat, Enter balloon, Worship Object

1026.text: FirewarriorFirewarriors are created by training Braves or any other Follower in the Firewarrior Training Hut. These Followers are slower and weaker in hand to hand combat than Warriors. They do, however, have the ability to cast the Blast spell and they can target buildings or the Enemy Followers from a distance. Like Warriors, they will not perform any menial tasks, such as construction, and are best suited to Guarding or Fighting.LifeStrengthBlast StrengthAbilitiesGuarding, fightingList of possible commandsWalk to point, Attack Enemy, Attack Enemy building, Enter Hut, Guard, Enter boat, Enter balloon, Worship Object

1027.text: PreacherPreachers are created by training Braves or any other Follower in the Temple. When Preachers are standing idle, they worship your name and chant passages from your Holy Scriptures. If an Enemy Follower hears them, they will be entranced and will sit and listen to the Preacher praising your name. After a while, without interruption, the Enemy Follower will be converted to your cause. Preachers will not perform construction tasks and, although you can command them to guard, they will only preach when an Enemy Follower approaches. They are happiest when extolling your word but do not have any effect on the Enemy Shaman or Preachers.LifeStrengthAbilitiesPreachingList of possible commandsWalk to point, Attack Enemy, Attack Enemy building, Enter Hut, Guard, Enter boat, Enter balloon, Worship Object

1028.text: SpySpies are created by training Braves or any other Follower in the Spy Training Hut. They are subversive Followers who can disguise themselves as the Enemy and then use this ability to sabotage Enemy buildings. To do this, first select one or more of your Spies. Then, choose which player colour you want to disguise them as and click on the same coloured Disguise Icon on the Control Panel.Your Spy will then don the clothes of the Enemy, although your Followers will ignore him. You can then send him into Enemy territory without fear of attack.To sabotage a building, simply select one or more of your Spies and left-click on an Enemy building. They will then walk to the building and set it alight.To unmask a suspected Enemy Spy, you can do a number of things. If an Enemy Spy passes one of your Spies or passes a Guard Tower with one of your Spies inside, he will be seen and unmasked. If your Followers catch an Enemy Spy whilst he is sabotaging, they will automatically attack him. If you see a disguised Enemy Spy, whether he is in your settlement or not, move your mouse over him and right-click to blow his cover.LifeStrengthAbilitiesSpyingList of possible commandsWalk to point, Attack Enemy, Attack Enemy building, Enter Hut, Guard, Enter boat, Enter balloon, Sabotage, Worship Object

1029.text: Command ListWalk to pointAttack EnemyAttack Enemy buildingConstruct BuildingEnter HutGather woodPick up woodGuardEnter boatEnter balloonSabotage BuildingWorship Object

1030.text: Walk To PointThis command tells your selected Followers to move to a certain point on the landscape. This command is automatically available when your mouse pointer is over an empty piece of ground and you have one or more Followers selected.To Use: Select one or more of your Followers. Move your mouse pointer to the place on the ground you want them to move to and left-click.

1031.text: Attack EnemyThis command tells your selected Followers to attack the Enemy Follower currently under your mouse pointer. This command is automatically available when you put your mouse pointer over an Enemy Follower and you have one or more Followers selected.To Use: Select one or more of your Followers. Move your mouse pointer over the Enemy Follower you want to attack and left-click.

1032.text: Attack Enemy BuildingThis command tells your selected Followers to attack and demolish the Enemy building currently under the mouse pointer. This command is automatically available when you put your mouse pointer over an Enemy building and you have one or more Followers selected.To Use: Select one or more of your Followers. Then move your mouse pointer to the Enemy building you want to attack and left-click.

1033.text: Construct BuildingThis command tells your selected Braves to construct the Plan currently under your mouse pointer. This command is automatically available when you put your mouse over a Plan or an uncompleted building and you have one or more Braves selected.To Use: Select one or more of your Braves. Then move your mouse pointer to the Plan or building you want to construct and left-click.

1034.text: Enter HutThis command tells your selected Followers to enter the Hut currently under your mouse pointer. This command is automatically available when you put your mouse pointer over a fully constructed Hut and you have one or more Followers selected.To Use: Select one or more of your Followers. Then move your mouse pointer to the Hut you want them to enter and left-click.

1035.text: Gather WoodThis command tells your selected Braves to gather Wood from the Tree currently under your mouse pointer. This command is automatically available when you put your mouse pointer over a Tree and you have one or more Braves selected.To Use: Select one or more of your Braves. Then move your mouse pointer to the Tree you want them to gather Wood from and left-click.

1036.text: Pick Up WoodThis command tells your selected Braves to pick up the Wood currently under your mouse pointer. This command is automatically available when you put your mouse pointer over a pile of Wood and you have one or more Braves selected.To Use: Select one or more of your Braves. Then move your mouse pointer to the pile of Wood you want to pick up and left-click.

1037.text: GuardThis command tells your selected Followers to guard around the Guard Post currently under your mouse pointer and attack any approaching Enemy. This command is automatically available when you put your mouse pointer over a Guard Post and you have one or more Followers selected.To Use: Select one or more of your Followers. Then move your mouse pointer to the Guard Post you want them to guard around and left-click. You can also command your Followers to Guard around your Shaman. To do this, select one or more of your Followers; then move your mouse pointer over the Shaman and left-click. They will then Guard around her and attack any Enemy who approaches.

1038.text: Enter BoatThis command tells your selected Followers to board the Boat currently under your mouse pointer. This command is automatically available when you put your mouse pointer over a Boat and you have one or more Followers selected.To Use: Select one or more of your Followers. Then move your mouse pointer to the Boat you want them to board and left-click.

1039.text: Enter BalloonThis command tells your selected Followers to board the Balloon currently under your mouse pointer. This command is automatically available when you put your mouse pointer over a Balloon and you have one or more Followers selected.To Use: Select one or more of your Followers. Then move your mouse pointer to the Balloon you want them to board and left-click.

1040.text: Sabotage BuildingThis command tells your selected Spies to Sabotage the Enemy building currently under your mouse pointer. This command is automatically available when you put your mouse pointer over an Enemy building and you have one or more Spies selected.To Use: Select one or more of your Spies. Then move your mouse pointer to the Enemy building you want them to Sabotage and left-click.

1041.text: Worship ObjectThis command tells your selected Followers to worship the Stone Head, Totem Pole or enter a Vault of Knowledge currently under your mouse pointer. This command is automatically available when you put your mouse pointer over a one of these objects and you have one or more Followers selected.To Use: Select one or more of your Followers. Then move your mouse pointer to the object you want them to worship and left-click.

1042.text: Magical ShieldMagical Shield casts a protective magical shell over any Follower it is cast upon. That Follower will be invulnerable to the effects of many spells including Blast and Lightning.To Use: Left-click to select the Magical Shield Spell from the Spells Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell. Left-click to fire.RangeMana Used

1043.text: TeleportTeleport is a special spell which only the Shaman can use. It has an unlimited range and when you cast it on a point on the land, the Shaman will teleport to that point.To Use: Left-click to select the Teleport Spell from the Spells Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to teleport the Shaman. Left-click to fire.RangeUnlimited Range

1044.text: BloodlustBloodlust, when cast on your own Followers, will turn them into frenzied killing machines, capable of successfully battling enemies more powerful than themselves.To Use: Left-click to select the Bloodlust Spell from the Spells Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell. Left-click to fire.Range

1045.text: ArmageddonArmageddon is the ultimate weapon and should not be used lightly. When you cast the spell, an arena will rise from the earth and every Follower on the world will be teleported to it. Then, an almighty battle will begin between all the tribes and the last tribe standing will be the conqueror of the world.To Use: Left-click to select the Armageddon Spell from the Spells Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell and build the arena. Left-click to fire.RangeUnlimited Range

1046.text: The Control PanelThe Map and the World ViewCommandee ToggleShamanQuery ButtonEnemy Tribes IconsTotal FollowersSpell Charge RateBuildings PanelSpells PanelFollowers Panel

1047.text: The Map and the World ViewMapThis is the Scanner Map. It gives you a bird's eye view of the world. On it, you can see the sea and land and also your people. You cannot, however, see the Enemy (except when they are close to your Guard Towers) and you will need to use the World View if want to see them. If a fog is covering the world, there will also be a fog on the map. In the centre of the map is a circle indicating where you are on the world. Around this circle is a white arrow which points to north. To zoom to a point, left-click on the map. To go to the World View, right-click on the map.Wildmen: Grey dotsYour Followers: Small blue dotsYour Shaman: Large blue dotYour buildings: Dark blue dotsWorld ViewThe World View is a more detailed map and also gives you information about the Enemy. You can get to it by either Right Clicking on the Scanner Map or pressing Return. Like the Scanner Map, you can see the land and your Followers, but now you can also see the Enemy Followers and buildings in their own colours. Your buildings appear as blue squares and the dots on the buildings indicate how many Followers are occupying them. Each of your Followers has a different shaped dot so that you can easily determine who is who. You can rotate the map with the Cursor Keys and also (if you have a middle mouse button) middle-click and drag. If you right-click anywhere on the globe, you will zoom back down to the ground at that point. Pressing Return will simply take you back down to the ground.

1048.text: Zoom To FightWhen any of your Followers are involved in a battle, this icon will flash. By Left Clicking on the icon, you will be zoomed to that battle. If there are multiple battles going on at any one time, repeated clicks on the icon will cycle through them.

1049.text: Commandee ToggleThe Commandee Toggle icon is directly related to the Total Followers icons and is discussed in more detail there.

1050.text: ShamanThe Shaman icon is similar to those on the Follower Panel and allows you to directly access the Shaman without scrolling around the world looking for her. You can see exactly what the Shaman is currently doing by watching her on the icon. To the right of the icon is the Shaman's health bar. You can left-click on the icon to select her and right-click on the icon to zoom to her.

1051.text: Query ButtonThe Query Button allows you to go directly to a section of this Encyclopaedia by clicking on a specific icon or object. To use, left-click on the icon and your mouse pointer will change to a question mark. You can then left-click on any icon or object on the screen and go straight to its explanation in the Encyclopaedia.

1052.text: Enemy Tribes IconsThe Enemy Tribes icons perform a number of different functions. They only appear if there are enemies of that colour on the world. If the icons flash, it means that one of the Followers of that Enemy is dying and you can use it as an indication of whom is fighting whom.You also use the icons to disguise your Spies. To do this, select one or more of your Spies and left-click on the colour you want them to become. They will then disguise themselves and you can use them against the Enemy.In multiplayer games, you can ally with another player. If you hold down Shift and left-click on the player's Enemy Tribe Icon, it will become inverted. Then, all your Followers will ignore that player's Followers unless directly commanded to attack. To completely ally, the other player must also Shift left-click on your Enemy Tribe Icon. If they do not, their Followers will still automatically attack yours.

1053.text: Total FollowersThe Total Followers section of the Control Panel is closely related to the Followers Panel. The first icon is the total number of Followers overall. The red bar indicates how many Followers you have compared to how many your buildings can handle. If the red bar reaches the top, you will have run out of accommodation and you will not breed any more Followers without constructing more Huts. You can only have a maximum population of two hundred Followers. Once this maximum has been reached, you will not be able to breed any more Braves and convert any Wildmen or Enemy Followers. The rest of the icons display how many Followers you currently have of that type.The Commandee Toggle icon above the Total Followers section toggles the Total Followers numbers between all of those Followers on the world and all of the Followers visible on the screen. For example, if you turn the Commandee Toggle on, you will only be able to select those Braves immediately near you. If you turn the Commandee Toggle back off, you will be able to select all the Braves on the world. This can be very useful if the only Followers you want to select are the Followers from a certain part of the world.To select one type of Follower, left-click on the icon. To select five Followers of a type, hold down Ctrl and left-click on the icon. To select all the Followers of a type, hold down Shift and left-click on the icon. To zoom to and cycle through all the Followers of a type, right-click on the icon.

1054.text: Buildings PanelThe Buildings Panel lists all the buildings currently available for you to construct. To select a building, left-click on the icon. To zoom to and cycle through all the buildings of that type, right-click on the icon. If there is a question mark icon on the panel, it means that the building is hidden on the level either in a Stone Head or a Vault of Knowledge.

1055.text: Spells PanelThe Spells Panel lists all the Spells currently available for you to cast. To select a spell, left-click on the icon. Each spell uses Mana and needs to be charged before you can use it. The blue bar on the icon indicates how much more Mana you currently have saved in that spell. This bar needs to be filled before you can cast the spell. The dots on the icon indicate the maximum number of shots of the spell you can have charged at once. As each spell finishes charging, a blue dot will appear on the icon and you will be able to cast that spell. One Shot spells, given by the Stone Heads, are shown by red dots. More powerful spells take longer to charge so you can prevent a spell from charging by Right Clicking on its icon. This means that more Mana will be available for other spells, increasing their charge rate. To toggle all the spells on or off, hold down Shift and right-click on any icon. If you hold down Ctrl and right-click on a spell's icon, you will toggle all except that spell on or off.If there is a question mark icon on the panel, it means that the spell is hidden on the level either in a Stone Head or a Vault of Knowledge.The Spells Panel is also used for the Forge World option, if it is chosen at the start of multiplayer games.

1056.text: Followers PanelThe Followers Panel is a table of all your Followers performing various tasks. The first line lists Followers currently selected. The second line lists those Followers who are not currently working. The third line lists Followers in buildings. The fourth line lists those Followers working, such as constructing or guarding. The fifth and sixth lines are different and list those Boats and Balloons with Followers inside. If you select a Follower in a vehicle, you also select the vehicle, therefore each column shows the number of vehicles with at least one of that type of Follower inside.You can perform any of the following selections on a icon with a number on. To select one of the type, left-click on the icon. To select five of a type, hold down Ctrl and left-click on the icon. To select all of a type, hold down Shift and left-click on the icon. To zoom to and cycle through all, right-click on the icon.

1057.text: Information on this item is unavailable because you haven't discovered it yet.

1058.text: ManaMana is an ethereal force created by your Followers. With it you can charge up any of your spells and train your Followers. Braves create Mana when working or resting in Huts. See the Spells Panel for more information on how to use Mana to your advantage.

1059.text: Spell Charge RateThe Spell Charge Rate bar shows the rate at which your spells are begin charged with Mana. The lower the white bar, the longer your spells will take to charge and the longer your Followers will take to train. You can increase the rate by charging fewer spells, training fewer Followers, giving work to idle Followers or breeding more Braves.If the bar rises into the green, your spells are charging at the maximum rate.If the bar flashes red, you are wasting mana and should charge up some of your inactive spells.To learn more about charging spells, see the Spells Panel section.

1060.text: Forge World Panel and SpellsThe Forge World option is only available at the start of multiplayer games. If the option is selected, you are given a number of Single Shot Spells at your command, each explained below, to mould the world before to battle commences. The Shaman is not present during this time so you can cast the spells anywhere on the world. A clock in the corner of the screen counts the time before the game starts.You can also raise and lower small areas of the landscape. To raise land, hold down Alt and left-click. To lower land, hold down Alt and right-click.ErodeFlattenLandbridgeHillValleyRaiseLowerWildmenTrees

1061.text: ErodeThe Erode spell accelerates time and reshapes the earth as if a thousand years of rain and snow were weathering and reshaping the landscape.To Use: Left-click to select the Erode spell from the Forge World Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell. Left-click to fire.

1062.text: FlattenFlatten is a powerful land-altering spell which, when cast on a piece of land, will spread out and level the land around to the same height as the point it was cast on.To Use: Left-click to select the Flatten spell from the Forge World Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell. Left-click to fire.

1063.text: LandbridgeThe Landbridge spell evens out the land from a point at the bottom of your screen to where it is cast. You can use the spell to create causeways across otherwise impassible rivers or to level towering mountains.To Use: Left-click to select the Landbridge spell from the Forge World Panel. Rotate and move the land so that the spot from where you want to cast the spell is at the bottom of the screen. Move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell and left-click to fire.

1064.text: HillThis spell creates a small, dome-shaped hill where it is cast.To Use: Left-click to select the Hill Spell from the Forge World Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell. Left-click to fire.

1065.text: ValleyValley creates a bowl-like depression in the land where it is cast.To Use: Left-click to select the Valley spell from the Forge World Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell. Left-click to fire.

1066.text: RaiseRaise slowly elevates the area of land where the spell was cast.To Use: Left-click to select the Raise spell from the Forge World Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell. Left-click to fire.

1067.text: LowerLower causes the area of land where the spell was cast to slowly sink.To Use: Left-click to select the Lower spell from the Forge World Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell. Left-click to fire.

1068.text: WildmenThis spell creates some Wildmen wherever it is cast.To Use: Left-click to select the Wildmen spell from the Forge World Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell. Left-click to fire.

1069.text: TreesThis spell creates some Trees wherever it is cast.To Use: Left-click to select the Trees spell from the Forge World Panel and move the mouse pointer to where you want to target the spell. Left-click to fire.

1070.text: ObeliskObelisks are similar to Totem Poles but can only be worshipped by the Shaman. If you right-click on the Obelisk, you will see that only the Shaman is required to worship it.To worship an Obelisk, select the Shaman and left-click on the stone. If you right-click on the stone again, you will see a red line next to the Shaman icon and this indicates how long it will take.
